html:
SMTO-HTTP-0070 — SMTO was given two different ways to sign in to a service

GUID: 6acfe728-c0ff-4b1b-91ef-5090fb9bcebc
Slug: http-auth-selector-conflict
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to reach a web service using a saved connection and separate sign-in details at the same time, so it stopped. Nothing was sent to the service.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, tell SMTO the name of the saved connection to use (as shown in Parameter Store) and ask it not to add separate sign-in details. A saved connection already holds its own sign-in details, so a second set makes it unclear which account to use.
  2. If you meant to use one-time sign-in details instead, ask SMTO to connect with those details only and leave the saved connection out. One-time sign-in details are accepted only when no saved connection is chosen for the same request.
  3. If it stops again, open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The details show which step asked for both sign-in methods.

What success looks like

  • The step reaches the service and shows a result instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO's saved connections. Don't paste passwords or tokens into the conversation, and don't copy sign-in details from one saved connection into another.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The HTTP request/connect capability rejected the call because it combined a saved profile_key or connection_ref with inline one-off auth.

What this means

  • One-off authentication is supplied together with a saved profile/connection authentication source. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • One-off authentication is supplied together with a saved profile/connection authentication source.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify which selector owns the intended account and remove the unintended authentication source.

How to fix it

  • Send exactly one authentication source per call: connection_ref, profile_key, or inline auth with base_url. The check runs in http.request, http.connect and gateway_core.http_contract.prepare_request before dispatch; do not merge credentials across saved profiles.
  • Choose one intended authentication source and remove the other selector. Do not merge credentials across profiles.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • One explicit authentication source passes ordinary profile and origin checks.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
